newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia wants telecoms shares placed abroad.
newsitem.headline: Russia wants telecoms shares placed abroad.

text.p: Russia plans to place shares in its telecommunications companies abroad, and is already working on a New York listing, communication minister Vladimir Bulgak said on Friday.
"We are working in this direction very patiently, very persistently, as the share trading law requirements of other countries very tough," Bulgak told a news conference.
He said he expected level-three American Depositary Receipts of Vympel-Kommunikatsii (Vympelkom) to be listed on the New York Stock Exchange at the beginning of November.
"But one company is too few, we need more," Bulgak said.

Cellular telecoms company Vympelkom, which operates under the name Bee-Line, said at the end of September that it had filed a request to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to place its ADRs in the United States and Canada and list them on the New York Stock Exchange -- making it the first Russian company to be listed on Wall Street.
The communications ministry expects the ADRs will cover 3.92 million ordinary Vympelkom shares, it said in a statement.
Bulgak said the ministry had ordered all telecommunications companies to transfer to international accounting standards within two years.
He also said that a unified registry for all Russian telecoms companies - Registrator-Svyaz - would soon start working.
